cards.title: Continuum Dirac Hamiltonian with intrinsic spin orbit mass
cards.role: bulk QSH spectrum and intrinsic gap
cards.latex: H=hbar v_F(sigma_x tau_z q_x + sigma_y q_y) + Delta_so sigma_z tau_z s_z; E=+/-sqrt((hbar v_F q)^2 + Delta_so^2)

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf pp. 1-2, Eqs. (2)-(3) and following paragraph

cards.numerical_form: direct 4x4 continuum diagonalization and analytic eigenvalues

checks.reason: The Hamiltonian and dispersion are printed explicitly.
Mutually anticommuting Dirac matrices square to (hbar vF q)^2 + Delta_so^2.

cards.title: First-star microscopic matrix projection
cards.role: derive the intrinsic mass matrix before the scalar bare-gap estimate

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf p. 4, Eq. (7) and first-star paragraph

derived_from: three equivalent reciprocal-space corners per valley
cards.numerical_form: explicit Hermitian 8x8 plane-wave matrix in sublattice-valley-spin order

checks.reason: Eq. (7) and the adjacent first-star paragraph explicitly print the scalar coefficient and sigma_z tau_z s_z structure.
The explicit matrix matches (2 pi^2/3a^3) sigma_z tau_z s_z within 8.9e-16 and has the required fourfold +/- spectrum.
The plane-wave cross product reverses sign under valley exchange and the sublattice phase reverses it between A and B.

open_questions: The paper explicitly calls the first-star result crude because detailed Bloch orbitals are not supplied.

cards.title: Finite-Rashba conventional spin-current Kubo proxy
cards.role: quantify a nonzero-Rashba response without inventing the externally cited conserved-spin operator

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf p. 2, paragraph following Eq. (5) and citation to Murakami et al., PRB 69, 235206

checks.reason: The paper explicitly states a weak-Rashba spin Hall correction but delegates the conserved-current definition to an external citation; the card therefore labels the implemented conventional current as a proxy.
The response is continuous from the quantized limit and changes by 0.25 percent at lambda_R/Delta_so=.05 while [H,s_z] is explicitly nonzero.

open_questions: The graphene paper does not print the cited conserved-spin operator; the conventional-current result is a declared proxy and cannot close that exact definition.

cards.title: One-loop Coulomb self-energy and SO vertex shell integrals
cards.role: derive both Eq. (8) coefficients independently of its closed solution
cards.latex: Sigma(k,Delta)=1/2 int_shell d^2q/(2pi)^2 (2pi e^2/q) [sigma dot(q+k)+Delta sigma_z]/sqrt(|q+k|^2+Delta^2)

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf p. 4, Fig. 3 and Eq. (8) discussion

derived_from: Pauli projections of finite differences in k and Delta
cards.numerical_form: Gauss-Legendre logarithmic radial integration and independent angular quadrature

checks.reason: Fig. 3 and Eq. (8) identify the Coulomb exchange and SO-vertex renormalizations whose coefficients are independently projected here.
The matrix projections recover the velocity coefficient 0.250000002 and SO-vertex coefficient 0.499999984 without inserting either number.
A five-shell sweep is linear in ell with slopes 1/4 and 1/2.

cards.title: Neutral-graphene static RPA screening
cards.role: test the paper's claim that screening preserves the long-range logarithm

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf p. 4, screening sentence preceding Eq. (8)

cards.numerical_form: six-point interband Lindhard integration with angular and ultraviolet-cutoff convergence, followed by an RPA power-law fit

checks.reason: The sentence immediately before Eq. (8) states that screening preserves the logarithmic long-range interaction.
The independently integrated polarization has power 0.9947 and coefficient within 0.0051 of 1/4; only then does the screened potential fit a -0.9971 power.
Halving the angular grid changes the coefficient by at most 4.8e-7 and doubling the ultraviolet cutoff changes it by at most 0.00255.

open_questions: The paper cites rather than prints the polarization derivation; this clean-room check uses the standard four-flavor static Dirac limit.

cards.title: Time-reversal-breaking intervalley mass interpolation proxy
cards.role: separate the uniform-field edge gap and generic broken-time-reversal proxy from the publication-underspecified microscopic bulk connection
cards.latex: M_QSH=sigma_z tau_z s_z; M_triv=sigma_z; M_bridge=sigma_x tau_x s_x
cards.numerical_form: the legacy two-segment intervalley proxy plus coarse/fine lattice scans and continuous Brillouin-zone minimization of a translation-preserving candidate assembled from printed terms

checks.reason: The parallel-field paragraph explicitly claims that breaking time reversal permits a gapped connection to a trivial insulator and gaps the edge.
The uniform edge Zeeman term opens the expected gap. The separate bulk bridge is T-odd and gapped but its tau_x factor fails primitive translation, so it is not claimed as a uniform-field mechanism.

A deterministic continuous optimizer finds a direct-gap closing below 1e-16 t in the minimal translation-preserving candidate assembled from the printed intrinsic-SO, Rashba, Zeeman and staggered terms; a coarse 24x24 grid would have produced a false positive.

open_questions: The paper does not print the additional symmetry-allowed microscopic terms needed to construct its claimed translation-preserving gapped bulk connection; the minimal candidate available from printed terms is falsified.

cards.title: Finite-cylinder helical spectral flow
cards.role: realize the Laughlin h/e spin pump with explicit levels
derived_from: helical edge dispersion on a periodic cylinder
minimal coupling to one axial flux quantum
cards.numerical_form: 101 flux values and 17 angular levels per helical branch

checks.reason: The Laughlin paragraph explicitly states the h/e flux insertion, pumped spin and finite-cylinder scale conditions.
One level crosses in each branch, the final spectrum is the initial spectrum shifted by one angular quantum, and the pumped spin is hbar.

open_questions: The paper prints inequalities L>xi and ramp time>hbar/Delta but no particular finite cylinder dimensions; dimensionless factors 20 are declared reconstruction choices.

The direct gap closes at lambda_R=Delta_so.

cards.title: Quantized spin Hall conductivity

checks.reason: The response is printed explicitly.

cards.latex: H=t sum_<ij>,alpha c_i,alpha^dagger c_j,alpha + i t2 sum_<<ij>>,alpha,beta nu_ij s^z_alpha,beta c_i,alpha^dagger c_j,beta; Delta_so=3 sqrt(3) t2

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf p. 2, Eq. (6); p. 3, Fig. 1 caption

cards.numerical_form: Hermitian Bloch ribbon matrix for both spin sectors

checks.reason: Hamiltonian, orientation and t2/t=.03 are printed.
nu_ji=-nu_ij makes the imaginary second-neighbour term Hermitian.
The periodic bulk gap is 6 sqrt(3) t2.

open_questions: The paper does not print the ribbon width or k sampling used for Fig. 1.

cards.title: Ballistic edge conductances

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf p. 3, Fig. 2 caption and transport discussion

cards.numerical_form: spin-resolved terminal transmission tensor and Landauer-Buttiker current solve

checks.reason: The conductance and current values are printed in the Fig. 2 caption and prose.

cards.title: First-star intrinsic spin-orbit estimate
cards.latex: 2 Delta_so=4 pi^2 e^2 hbar^2/(3 m^2 c^2 a^3) approximately 2.4 K

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf p. 4, Eq. (7) and first-star paragraph

checks.reason: The first-star estimate and 2.4 K result are printed on p. 4.
The expression has dimensions of energy and is converted to kelvin through k_B.

open_questions: The estimate is explicitly described as crude and depends on the first-star approximation.

cards.title: Perpendicular-field Rashba estimate
cards.role: lambda_R much smaller than intrinsic gap
cards.latex: lambda_R=hbar v_F e E_z/(4 m c^2) approximately 0.5 mK for E_z approximately 50 V/300 nm
derived_from: Pauli spin-orbit coupling in an external electric field
cards.numerical_form: SI-unit estimate with declared v_F reference range

checks.reason: The formula, electric field and 0.5 mK estimate are printed on p. 4.
Using v_F near 10^6 m/s gives the printed sub-millikelvin scale.

open_questions: The paper does not print the exact v_F used in the 0.5 mK rounding.

cards.title: Coulomb RG flow and self-consistent renormalized gap

source_refs.value: raw/paper.pdf p. 4, Eq. (8) and following paragraph

derived_from: matrix-valued Fock self-energy and spin-orbit vertex shell integrals
cards.numerical_form: positive scalar root in a common energy unit

checks.reason: The RG equations, integrated form and 15 K estimate are printed on p. 4.
Direct integration of the coupled flows yields the printed squared logarithm.
g0=.74, Lambda0=2 eV and bare full gap 2.4 K define a unique enhanced positive gap.

cards.title: Nearest-neighbour lattice Rashba hopping
cards.latex: H_R=i lambda_R sum_<ij> c_i^dagger [z dot (s cross d_ij)] c_j

checks.reason: The bond-vector Rashba term and lambda_R<Delta_so condition are printed explicitly.
Reversing the directed bond makes the imaginary spin hopping Hermitian.
The configured nonzero coupling changes the spectrum while full-matrix time reversal and the edge Kramers degeneracy remain within 1e-10.

Adaptive full-Brillouin-zone edge-overlap tracking resolves every declared lambda_R/Delta_so<1 zigzag and armchair branch across three increasing widths; nested 192-768 point grids bound the branch-location discretization error.

open_questions: The paper does not specify the finite strip width or a lattice-to-continuum normalization; the width and adaptive momentum grids therefore remain declared convergence choices rather than paper-exact presentation parameters.

cards.title: Time-reversal constraint on the edge scattering matrix
derived_from: antiunitary time reversal of incoming and outgoing Kramers partners
cards.numerical_form: singular-value null space of the linear 2x2 matrix constraint

checks.reason: The S-matrix constraint and its no-backscattering consequence are printed.
The independently solved constraint has a one-dimensional complex null space with zero off-diagonal entries and equal diagonals.

cards.title: Weak-interaction edge conductivity exponent
cards.latex: Delta=4; sigma proportional to u^{-2} T^{3-2 Delta}=u^{-2}T^{-5}
derived_from: four fermion fields of scaling dimension 1/2
two spatial derivatives of scaling dimension 1
second time moment of the finite-temperature edge correlator
cards.numerical_form: Grassmann time-reversal transform plus independent u/T Kubo-kernel sweep

checks.reason: Both Delta=4 and 3-2 Delta are printed.
The encoded operator gives Delta=4, and log-log fits of the numerical correlator sweep recover temperature exponent -5 and interaction exponent -2.
